_comment_: P4-A: per-seat capacity map. Replaces the legacy single '4 Devin workers' cap with per-provider + per-model caps, a RAM governor, and a metered-seat class so prepaid-quota seats are exhausted before paid-per-token ones.
_comment_order: Selection order (fleet-ops#3125): PRODUCT work (PI_PICK_ROLE=product, exported by pi-issue-run and pi-packet-run) orders every candidate seat by the rolling last-20-sessions PR-yield ledger (~/.local/state/pi-packet/seat-yield.json, written each tick by libexec/fleet-metrics-export.py from pi-issue session files) descending; ties break by class prepaid-quota -> metered -> free so prepaid subs still drain first among equal performers, and a seat with fewer than 20 measured sessions gets provisional yield 0.5. Keystone/senior-review picks keep the prepaid order. Scout/canary/audit picks (any other PI_PICK_ROLE) stay free-first: free lanes (free_providers_in_order), then prepaid-quota (prepaid_providers_in_order, round-robin), then metered. cursor keystone/senior-review only at ~$16/day — #1133/#1167. Implemented in seat-lib.sh pick_seat; this file is data only. Classes are free / prepaid-quota / metered. subscription is accepted as an alias of prepaid-quota.
_comment_aimd: fleet-ops#424 re-lands AIMD; fleet-ops#3125 extends it to devin. Declared cap is the FLOOR. Free lanes (bai, commandcode, hetzner, opencode) set max_probe_ceiling above declared so pick_seat can admit cap+1 against a real 429/concurrency signal. Absent max_probe_ceiling means no upward probe (metered and non-devin prepaid default). hard_ceiling=true on ollama only: never probe, never back off below declared. devin is no longer a hard ceiling (2026-09-04, Nish 'cool with your suggestions' + expiry-first standing rule: the weekly sub was 97% unused, so a pinned floor wastes prepaid quota): provider max_probe_ceiling 8, per-model max_probe_ceiling on glm-5-2 (declared 3 / probe to 6) and swe-1-7 (declared 4 / probe to 8) via model-level AIMD. Learned state: ~/.local/state/pi-packet/learned-caps.json plus learned-caps-audit.log, owned by lib/seat-lib.sh; install.sh resets learned-caps.json when a deploy changes seat-caps.json so a stale learned cap never pins a raised declared floor. orcarouter stays cap=0 (dated 402) so it does not probe.
_comment_product_order: product_order=yield (fleet-ops#3125). The 2026-08-27 volume front-of-ladder (volume_providers_in_order, deleted in this change) routed every product pick to the volume prefix first; the measured sessions->PR yield on that order was 52-56% pass@1 while the best lane held 90%. Expiry-first still applies inside ties via the class rank (prepaid drains before metered, metered before free at equal yield).
_comment_ram_governor: 0.5 = raised 2026-08-28 (fleet-ops#1558) under per-repo MemoryMax drop-ins. Prior 0.6 was measured 2026-08-27 (fleet-ops#1168: 10 live workers, subtrees ~470MB total, 11.5GB MemAvailable under load, p95 per-worker <0.5GB). #1558 live sample (n=4 workers, 2026-08-28 ~18:45 IST): fleet-ops light MemoryPeak 0.11-0.63G; 0509 browser E2E MemoryPeak 2.06-2.39G. Per-repo MemoryMax now bounds the light class at 1536M and the browser class at 3G, so the governor budgets the TYPICAL light worker (0.5G) and self-reduces when MemAvailable drops under browser load. Hard backstops remain (user-1000.slice MemoryHigh=12G, oomd 80%). Admission keeps cgroup memory.current. Historical class pin (fleet-ops#202): memory.current p95 was 822.6 MB vs process VmRSS ~35 MB — admission keeps cgroup memory.current, never RSS. Measured sustainable ceiling on this 16GB box at MemAvailable~12.6G with per=0.5: ram_governor_cap=20; quiet-box MemAvailable~14.5G reaches 24. True 25 needs MemAvailable>=15GB or a second box (Nish capacity fork). Re-measure with bin/ram-metric-compare (heartbeat section 14). History: ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-measurement.json. Changing ram_gb_per_worker also requires updating the scenario-4 assertion (and ok line) in tests/ram-metric-compare.test.sh in the same PR (fleet-ops#1190 — the #1168 drift where the config moved 1.5->0.6 but the test still locked 1.5).

_comment_worker_memory: fleet-ops#1558 Q1=A: per-repo MemoryMax/MemoryHigh written by intake as a per-instance drop-in (pi-issue@<repo>-<N>.service.d/memory.conf) before systemctl start. _comment_quota_bench: quota_bench_default_s (fleet-ops#90): fallback bench window in seconds used by seat-lib.sh mark_seat_quota_bench when a provider returns a quota/cap 429 whose error text carries NO explicit reset window. cline=604800 (ClinePass weekly cap), devin=900 (devin 15-min message rate limit). walled_comeback._comment: fleet-ops#1167: a walled free seat is never permanently excluded. pick_seat already skip-until-usable_at then fail-opens. walled_comeback._comment_quarantine: fleet-ops#1422: quarantine for runaway consecutive_failure_count. After quarantine_threshold CONSECUTIVE failures on the same wall class, the seat's wall grows exponentially from quarantine_floor_s (1h) doubling per failure, capped at quarantine_cap_s (24h) — instead of re-probing on the flat base interval (rate_limit_s=900 / transient_http 30s) forever. Source: pi-seat-health.json 2026-08-27T22:30:01Z — opencode/mimo-v2.5-free c=67 (http 429), opencode/muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free c=80 (http 500, usable_at already past so re-probed every cycle; c=149 by 2026-08-30). Threshold 20: stops a 30s-cadence seat within ~10min, a 15min-cadence seat within 5h. Floor 1h and 24h cap follow the issue wording and the fleet-ops#1362 SEAT_PARK_WALL_S precedent. A successful probe resets the count to 0, so the seat is cold only until one success, never permanent.
walled_comeback._comment_seat_dead: fleet-ops#2145: a corpse is seat_dead=true, not a walled seat. transient_http/rate_limit/cli_timeout/transient_other/empty_run at >= seat_dead_consecutive_threshold (25) CONSECUTIVE failures are corpses — the threshold sits above quarantine_threshold (20) so a seat is first parked behind the exponential wall (1422) and only declared dead if it keeps failing past 25. quota_exhausted (HTTP 402) whose observed_at is older than seat_dead_quota_age_s (24h) is a hard billing wall that has not cleared — a corpse needing billing repair, not another re-probe. Source: pi-seat-health.json 2026-08-30T00:30:04Z — opencode/muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free c=149 (http 500), minimax/MiniMax-M3 c=69 (http 402, usable_at +60m re-probed hourly). The router (seat_usable) already excludes seat_dead=true; the census/snapshot counts corpses as dead, not walled. Recovery: the seat-walled-probe weekly probe that was the recovery writer was deleted (fleet-ops#2394, 2026-08-30 machinery deletion review — 14-day 100% fail, zero issues filed, seat-transition duty overlaps fleet-seat-recovery + seat-lib comeback clocks). A corpse now re-enters only after manual repair (re-auth / provider recovery), surfaced by the FleetDeadCredentialSeats alert. fleet-ops#2327 (2026-08-30 heartbeat): the corpse is now TERMINAL on both sides — the extension reclassifies the ledger health_class to the terminal "corpse" class the moment seat_dead fires (transient_http no longer persists on a dead seat), and the read side (seat_usable + the pick_seat excluded set) treats seat_dead=true as an ABSOLUTE exclusion: a stale observed_at does NOT resurrect a corpse into the ladder (before this, the stale-observed fail-open re-admitted muse-spark between weekly probes and its count grew 80 -> 150 straight 500s). fleet-ops#2415 (2026-08-30 heartbeat): the retirement is now TERMINAL on the RECORD — the corpse ledger carries NO usable_at comeback clock. The 1422 quarantine cap (24h) is a wall for WALLED seats that may recover, never a retry schedule for a corpse; the heartbeat read muse-spark at c=150 with usable_at +24h as "still on a 24h retry cycle" consuming probe budget forever. writeSeatLedgerEntry clears usable_at the moment seat_dead fires (and each further failure keeps it null), so no reader (heartbeat, seat_usable, census) sees a corpse as scheduled for re-probe. Recovery stays manual-only.

_comment_credits: zenmux and openrouter both carry FREE lanes AND paid credits (Nish, 2026-08-25). class=metered records that, but seat-lib.sh computes class_of() and then ignores it - pick_seat buckets by literal provider name, so both currently sit in the FREE bucket and their credits can be spent as if free. free_providers_in_order is the only working control until that is fixed (fleet-ops#42): free lanes first, credit-bearing seats last.
_comment_grok: grok cap=0 (2026-08-26): SuperGrok's subscription covers the grok.com app and the grok CLI, NOT the x.ai API. pi reaching api.x.ai/v1 with the CLI's own OAuth token returns 403 'You have run out of credits or need a Grok subscription'. pi also has NO registered grok-cli adapter ('No API provider registered for api: grok-cli'), so the CLI route is not reachable from pi either. Raising this cap requires either x.ai API credits (money - Nish only) or a pi custom-provider extension wrapping the grok CLI. The credential half of fleet-ops#41 is the prevent side for the LIVE seat: bin/grok-token-refresh + grok-token-refresh.timer (4h) keep ~/.pi/agent/auth.json[xai-oauth] alive headlessly (no pty, no TTY) so the prepaid SuperGrok seat (fleet-ops#1163) does not age into a 401. Tracked in fleet-ops#41.
_comment_worker_env: fleet-ops#1587: per-repo Environment variables written as drop-in (pi-issue@<repo>-<N>.service.d/environment.conf) by intake. Limits test parallelism on browser-heavy repos so per-worker MemoryPeak stays under the lowered cap. vitest forks are the dominant cost (one per CPU by default, each loading the full app + D1 migrations); playwright workers drive browser-instance concurrency.
_comment_error_classes: fleet-ops#859: data-driven lane-fault registry. pi-issue-run iterates this map by trigger_order, calling _matcher_dispatch <matcher> <out> <err> once per class; the FIRST match fires its writer and stops (one writer wins, no double-bench). This replaces the former hard-coded quota-cap and 503-overload dispatch blocks, so a future lane-fault class is a config-only addition (a row in seat-caps.json + a matcher function + a case branch in _matcher_dispatch / _writer_dispatch), not a third copy of the three-file pattern. The writers keep their own provider-default resolution (quota_bench_default_s / 503_bench_default_s in the provider rows below); this map is dispatch wiring only, not the default-window value. spawn_fail and mid_session_death are NOT here: they have time-based guards (spawn_elapsed < SPAWN_FAIL_MAX_S / > SPAWN_FAIL_MAX_S) that the generic matcher contract cannot express, so they stay as explicit blocks in pi-issue-run.
